description: This topic explores how speakers and writers choose the right register, style, vocabulary and channel to communicate clearly, politely and effectively for a given audience and purpose.

mcq.questionText: In language study, the term 'register' best refers to which of the following?

options.text: The list of all words in a dictionary
The variety of language chosen to suit a particular situation, audience and purpose
The grammar rules of standard English
The pitch of a person's voice when speaking

mcq.explanation: Register is the variety or style of language a person selects to match the situation, the audience and the purpose of communication.

mcq.questionText: Which expression is the most formal way to begin a letter to the District Education Officer?

options.text: Hey there, how's it going?
Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to request...
What's up, just wanted to ask...
Yo, I need a favour...

mcq.explanation: A letter to an official requires formal register; 'Dear Sir/Madam' with a clear, respectful request is appropriate, while the others are casual or slang.

mcq.questionText: Informal or colloquial language is MOST appropriate in which of these situations?

options.text: Writing a job application letter
Presenting a speech at a national ceremony
Chatting with a close friend about the weekend
Writing an academic examination essay

mcq.explanation: Casual conversation between friends calls for informal, relaxed language; the other contexts require formal register.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of slang?

options.text: I am extremely tired this evening.
That movie was lit!
Kindly switch off the lights.
The meeting will commence at nine o'clock.

mcq.explanation: 'Lit' is informal slang meaning excellent or exciting; the other sentences use standard, more formal expressions.

mcq.questionText: When choosing words and tone, the writer should mainly consider the:

options.text: length of the longest word available
audience and the purpose of the message
number of pages required
colour of the paper used

mcq.explanation: Effective communicators match their vocabulary and tone to who will read or hear the message and why it is being sent.

mcq.questionText: The specialised vocabulary used by people in a particular profession or field is called:

options.text: slang
jargon
dialect
accent

mcq.explanation: Jargon is the technical or specialised language of a trade or profession, such as medical or legal terms.

mcq.questionText: In the communication process, the person who creates and sends the message is the:

options.text: receiver
channel
sender
feedback

mcq.explanation: The sender (or encoder) is the source who forms the message and transmits it to the receiver.

mcq.questionText: The response that the receiver gives back to the sender, showing whether the message was understood, is called:

options.text: feedback
noise
channel
encoding

mcq.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's reply or reaction, allowing the sender to know whether the message was received and understood.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence shows the clearest and most concise communication?

options.text: Due to the fact that it was raining, we did not go.
On account of the rain, the trip was postponed because of the weather.
We did not go because it was raining.
It being a rainy sort of day, the going did not take place at all.

mcq.explanation: Conciseness means expressing an idea in as few clear words as needed; option C states the same idea simply and directly.

mcq.questionText: An example of non-verbal communication is:

options.text: writing a letter
nodding the head to show agreement
reading a notice aloud
making a phone call

mcq.explanation: Non-verbal communication uses gestures, facial expressions and body language rather than words; nodding is a gesture.

mcq.questionText: Anything that interferes with or distorts a message during communication is called a:

options.text: channel
barrier
feedback
register

mcq.explanation: A communication barrier (such as noise, poor language or distraction) blocks or distorts the message between sender and receiver.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a feature that mainly belongs to spoken rather than written English?

options.text: Careful paragraphing
Use of tone of voice, pauses and gestures
Permanent record that can be re-read
Strict punctuation marks

mcq.explanation: Spoken English is supported by tone, pauses and gestures, while written English relies on punctuation and is permanent.

mcq.questionText: A sentence is said to be ambiguous when it:

options.text: is very short
can be understood in more than one way
uses only formal words
contains no verbs

mcq.explanation: Ambiguity occurs when a statement has two or more possible meanings, which can confuse the receiver.

mcq.questionText: Which channel would be MOST suitable for urgently informing a friend that the bus has been cancelled?

options.text: A handwritten letter sent by post
A notice on a school noticeboard
A phone call or text message
An article in next month's magazine

mcq.explanation: Urgent messages need a fast channel; a phone call or text message reaches the receiver immediately.

mcq.questionText: Standard English is BEST described as the variety of English that:

options.text: only uses slang and casual expressions
follows widely accepted grammar and is used in education and official settings
is spoken by only one small village
ignores rules of spelling and grammar

mcq.explanation: Standard English follows generally accepted rules of grammar, spelling and vocabulary and is used in schools, media and official communication.

fib.questionText: The variety of language chosen to suit a particular situation, audience and purpose is called _____.
fib.explanation: Register refers to the appropriate style or variety of language for a given context.

fib.questionText: Language that is relaxed and used among friends, often including slang, is described as _____ language.
fib.explanation: Informal (or colloquial) language is casual and suitable for friendly, everyday situations.

fib.questionText: The specialised technical vocabulary used within a particular profession or trade is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Jargon is the technical language understood mainly by people in a specific field.

fib.questionText: In the communication process, the path or medium through which a message travels is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The channel is the medium, such as speech, letter or telephone, that carries the message.

fib.questionText: The reply or reaction the receiver gives to show the message was understood is called _____.
fib.explanation: Feedback closes the communication loop by informing the sender of the receiver's response.

fib.questionText: Communication that uses gestures, facial expressions and body language instead of words is called _____ communication.
fib.explanation: Non-verbal communication conveys meaning through body language rather than spoken or written words.

fib.questionText: Expressing a message in as few clear words as necessary, without unnecessary repetition, is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Conciseness means being brief and to the point while still being clear.

fib.questionText: A sentence that can be understood in more than one way is said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Ambiguity should be avoided because it confuses the receiver about the intended meaning.

fib.questionText: Anything such as noise or distraction that interferes with the message between sender and receiver is a communication _____.
fib.explanation: A barrier blocks or distorts effective communication.

fib.questionText: The variety of English that follows widely accepted grammar rules and is used in schools and official documents is called _____ English.
fib.explanation: Standard English is the accepted form used in formal, educational and official settings.

tf.questionText: Register means choosing language that suits the situation, audience and purpose of communication.
tf.explanation: This is the correct definition of register.

tf.questionText: Slang is always appropriate in a formal job application letter.
tf.explanation: Formal documents require formal register; slang is inappropriate in a job application.

tf.questionText: Jargon may confuse readers who do not belong to the profession that uses it.
tf.explanation: Because jargon is specialised, outsiders may not understand it, so it should be avoided with a general audience.

tf.questionText: Feedback is part of the communication process that tells the sender whether the message was understood.
tf.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response showing how the message was received.

tf.questionText: Written English is usually more permanent and can be re-read, while spoken English is often immediate and supported by tone and gesture.
tf.explanation: Written language is recorded and lasting, whereas speech is supported by voice and body language.

tf.questionText: Politeness and courtesy are not important in effective communication.
tf.explanation: Politeness and courtesy help maintain good relationships and make the receiver more willing to respond positively.

tf.questionText: An ambiguous sentence has only one clear meaning.
tf.explanation: An ambiguous sentence has more than one possible meaning, which causes confusion.

tf.questionText: The same level of formality should be used whether you are writing to a friend or to a government official.
tf.explanation: Register should change with the audience; a friend allows informal language while an official requires formal language.

tf.questionText: Choosing the wrong channel, such as posting an urgent message in next month's magazine, can make communication ineffective.
tf.explanation: The channel must match the urgency and nature of the message for communication to succeed.

tf.questionText: Non-standard English, such as some local dialect forms, is generally not recommended in official examination answers.
tf.explanation: Formal and official contexts, including examinations, expect standard English.

summary.questionText: In one or two sentences, explain what 'register' means in communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Register is the variety or style of language a person chooses to match the situation, audience and purpose, for example using formal language for an official and informal language for a friend.
summary.explanation: A good answer defines register as situation-appropriate language choice and gives the idea of formal versus informal use.

summary.questionText: Briefly distinguish between formal and informal language and give one situation suited to each.
summary.correctAnswer: Formal language follows strict, polite and standard forms and suits official situations such as a letter to an officer, while informal language is relaxed and casual and suits friendly conversation with a close friend.
summary.explanation: The answer should contrast the two registers and match each to an appropriate context.

summary.questionText: List the main elements of the communication process in order.
summary.correctAnswer: The main elements are the sender, the message, the channel, the receiver and the feedback.
summary.explanation: These five elements describe how a message moves from source to receiver and back as feedback.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between verbal and non-verbal communication, with one example of each.
summary.correctAnswer: Verbal communication uses spoken or written words, for example a telephone conversation, while non-verbal communication uses gestures, facial expressions and body language, for example nodding to show agreement.
summary.explanation: A correct answer separates word-based communication from body-language communication and gives an example of each.

summary.questionText: Why should jargon be used carefully when communicating with a general audience?
summary.correctAnswer: Jargon is specialised technical language understood mainly by people in a particular field, so using it with a general audience may confuse readers who do not know those terms.
summary.explanation: The answer should note that jargon limits understanding for non-specialists.

summary.questionText: Mention two qualities of effective written communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Effective written communication should be clear and concise, and it should avoid ambiguity while using an appropriate register and polite tone.
summary.explanation: Acceptable qualities include clarity, conciseness, correctness, politeness and freedom from ambiguity.

summary.questionText: Give two examples of barriers to effective communication.
summary.correctAnswer: Examples of barriers include noise or distraction, use of difficult language or jargon, poor handwriting, language differences and lack of attention from the receiver.
summary.explanation: Any two genuine barriers that distort or block a message are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Explain why choosing the right channel is important, using one example.
summary.correctAnswer: Choosing the right channel ensures the message reaches the receiver in good time and form; for example, an urgent message should be sent by phone call or text rather than by slow postal letter.
summary.explanation: The answer should link channel choice to the message's purpose and urgency with an example.

summary.questionText: How do politeness and courtesy improve communication?
summary.correctAnswer: Politeness and courtesy show respect for the receiver, create goodwill and make the receiver more willing to listen and respond positively, which makes communication more effective.
summary.explanation: The answer should connect courteous language to better relationships and cooperation.

summary.questionText: State two differences between spoken and written English.
summary.correctAnswer: Spoken English is immediate and supported by tone of voice, pauses and gestures, while written English is more permanent, can be re-read and depends on punctuation and careful organisation.
summary.explanation: Acceptable differences include permanence, use of tone or gesture, immediacy and reliance on punctuation.

hoq.questionText: A student writes to the head teacher: 'Hi boss, gimme a day off coz am tired.' Which revision best fixes the register for this formal request?

options.text: 'Yo head teacher, I really need a break, you know how it is.'
'Dear Sir/Madam, I kindly request permission to be absent for one day as I am unwell.'
'Hey, can I skip school tomorrow? Thanks a lot, mate.'
'Boss, am tired so I wont come, ok?'

hoq.explanation: A request to the head teacher needs formal register, a respectful greeting and a clear reason; option B meets these requirements while the others remain casual or use slang.

hoq.questionText: A health officer must explain a vaccine to villagers who are not medical experts. Which approach best ensures effective communication?

options.text: Use heavy medical jargon to sound professional
Speak only in a foreign language the audience does not know
Use simple, clear standard language and check understanding through feedback
Read a long technical report quickly without pausing

hoq.explanation: Effective communication adapts vocabulary to the audience and invites feedback; simple, clear language with confirmation of understanding suits non-specialist villagers, while jargon and unfamiliar language create barriers.

hoq.questionText: The notice 'Visitors must not enter the lab without a teacher present at all times' is unclear. Which version removes the ambiguity most effectively?

options.text: 'Visitors lab teacher present must not enter at all times.'
'Visitors may enter the laboratory only when a teacher is present.'
'No visitors lab unless maybe a teacher around sometimes.'
'Visitors and teachers must not enter the laboratory at all times.'

hoq.explanation: Clarity requires one unmistakable meaning; option B states plainly that a teacher's presence is the condition for entry, removing the ambiguity of the original notice.
